amendment.no_extension: 192 from the start. No peeking and extending. If it fails at 192, it fails.
amendment.why: the natural replicate in the search archive (identical genome, different development seeds, delta_G +0.375 vs +0.156) implies SD(d) ~0.875. At a true delta_G near the candidate's 0.219, the payoff gate has only ~0.47 power at n=64, binding on LCB95>0. Running 64 and later being tempted to extend is worse than starting at 192.
amendment.prospective: no confirmation episode has been run under this protocol and no outcome exists, so the change cannot have been influenced by a result
amendment.not_a_rescue: raising n moves no threshold and cannot manufacture a pass. More episodes reduce false negatives without increasing type-I error.

both_poles_prospective.ruling: run BOTH poles prospectively under the identical confirmation protocol at n=192
both_poles_prospective.why: OBSERVABILITY_V2 was invented AFTER the OP7 episodes were observed. Its reading of OP7 (p_C 0.875, LCB95 0.750) is retrospective with respect to the V2 definition. V3_STRATEGIC_DEMAND must not rest on one pole's concealment being prospective and the other's being post-hoc.
both_poles_prospective.old_OP7_result_status: NOT discarded. It becomes prior independent replication. If OP7 passes again, the BREACH pole is supported by two separate blocks.
both_poles_prospective.same_block_for_both_poles: intentional: gives experimental symmetry across the two poles
both_poles_prospective.deeper_reason: the claim is uncertainty between conflicting strategic contexts. If A conceals but B announces itself early, a capable policy could infer A by elimination: clear B signal -> BREACH, no B signal -> A -> GUARD. The 'planning is required' argument needs BOTH sides of the fork to resist trivial early identification.

the_four_prospective_tests.conjunction: all four required. If one component fails, the whole claim fails exactly as preregistered.
